title: Passage and Current
premise: Bram Kavanagh, a salvage diver haunted by a navy wreck he was ordered to forget, is drifting through the Coral Sea when a dying prospector named Elias Wren trades him a map to a sunken bullion cache for one promise: see it found, or see it destroyed. The map draws the attention of Mara Voss, a maritime insurance investigator whose duty-bound pursuit of Bram collides with her growing love for him and her own doubts about the law she serves. Hunted by Voss's employer — a shipping magnate using the company as cover for his own salvage operation — Bram, Mara, and the ragtag crew of the leaking trawler Pelican must survive the monsoon season, betrayal, and a final dive on the wreck that started it all. In the end, they sink the evidence of the magnate's crimes rather than claim the gold, choosing justice outside the law, and choose each other over the lives they were running from.
about_author: I. M. Thackeray spent a decade working charter boats out of Far North Queensland before turning to fiction, and writes about salt, rust, and stubborn people with an insider's ear. Passage and Current is the third novel credited to the pen name, following two well-reviewed sea adventures.

chapters.title: The Wreck They Don't Name
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Diving a restricted navy site off Thursday Island, Bram recovers something he shouldn't — a stamped case with serial numbers — and burns it rather than report it. We learn he keeps moving because the last crew who stayed got silenced. Emotional beat: guilt and vigilance; a man who trusts no harbor.

chapters.title: A Dying Man's Bargain
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. In a Port Moresby tavern, prospector Elias Wren, shot and fading, presses a oilskin-wrapped map into Bram's hands: coordinates to the Meridian Star's lost bullion, plus a name — Halloran Shipping. His price: a promise. Bram gives it, not knowing what it will cost. Beat: reluctant oath, first hook of fate.

chapters.title: The Investigator
chapters.summary: Mara Voss's POV. In Brisbane, insurance investigator Mara Voss flags a fraudulent salvage claim tied to Halloran Shipping. Her boss, Aldous Crane, assigns her to find 'a diver named Kavanagh' — quietly, off the books. She senses the assignment is wrong but obeys. Beat: dutiful woman on a path she doesn't yet question.

chapters.title: Salt and Small Debts
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Aboard the battered trawler Pelican, Bram meets its found-family crew: gruff skipper Nell Okonkwo, engineer Tui, and deckhand Pili, a teenage stowaway. He hires on as diver to pay his passage north, hiding the map. Beat: warmth he resists feeling; the found family begins to form around him.

chapters.title: Following the Paper Trail
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara traces the fraud through Halloran's ledgers to a pattern of ships 'lost' where no storm was logged. Crane warns her off; she digs anyway. She finds Bram's old navy service record — redacted, then sealed. Beat: curiosity hardening into resolve; the reader sees Crane's shadow lengthen.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The Pelican takes a charter job that turns out to be a Halloran survey vessel scouting the same coordinates. Bram recognizes the ship from the tavern, realizes Wren's killers are close, and urges Nell to run ahead of the monsoon. Beat: paranoia justified; the chase begins.

chapters.title: Two Currents Meet
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara catches up to the Pelican at a refueling dock in Cairns, posing as a marine surveyor. She and Bram circle each other with careful lies — and an inconvenient spark. Tui quietly clocks her forged papers. Beat: attraction sharpened by mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Map Shows
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A Halloran strike team boards the Pelican at night hunting the map. In the fight, Pili is hurt and the truth comes out: Bram shows Nell the chart and tells her about Wren's promise. Instead of putting him ashore, Nell plots a course for the coordinates. Beat: trust extended; family chosen.

chapters.title: The Long Reach of Halloran
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara confronts Crane with what she's found; he reveals the magnate Edmund Halloran has been running ghost-salvage for years and that her investigation was meant to find a scapegoat — Bram. Ordered to bring him in, she instead burns her report. Beat: duty cracks; she crosses her first line.

chapters.title: Running Before the Monsoon
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The Pelican runs north through building weather with a Halloran gunboat behind and a leaking hull below. Mara, exposed as an investigator, offers her skills instead of apologies; Bram lets her aboard fully. Beat: enemies becoming allies under pressure; romance kindles honestly.

chapters.title: The Lagoon
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. They shelter in a hidden reef lagoon to patch the hull. Quiet chapter: Tui teaches Mara to splice line, Pili tells Bram why she ran from home, and Bram almost tells Mara about the navy wreck and stops himself. Beat: tenderness and the secret still between them.

chapters.title: Crane's Net
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Crane, furious at her betrayal, leaks Mara's identity to Halloran's men and puts a warrant out in her name too. Now fugitives together, she and Bram stop pretending. She confesses her original orders; he forgives her — mostly. Beat: both stripped of their old lives; nothing left but forward.

chapters.title: First Dive on the Meridian
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. At the coordinates, Bram and Mara dive the Meridian Star and find the bullion hold — and evidence chained beside it: manifests proving Halloran scuttled his own ships with crews aboard. Bram recognizes the stamp from the navy wreck. It's the same operation, years earlier. Beat: horror and revelation; the promise becomes personal.

chapters.title: The Navy Knows
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A navy patrol boat intercepts them; Bram is detained and interrogated by an officer who once signed his silence order. Mara bargains with half-truths to get him released, realizing the navy buried the Meridian to protect Halloran. Beat: the law itself revealed as complicit; justice must come from elsewhere.

chapters.title: Pili's Choice
chapters.summary: Pili's POV. Sent ashore to buy parts, Pili is cornered by Halloran's men and offered money to betray the crew's position. She takes the cash — and feeds them false coordinates, then races back to warn the Pelican. Beat: the youngest member proves her place in the family; loyalty tested and kept.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Anchor
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Halloran's gunboat finds them anyway — tipped off by Tui, who took payment to cover debts back home. In the boarding fight, Nell is shot and the map seized. Tui, seeing Nell bleeding, turns on Halloran's men and pays for it. Beat: betrayal and sacrifice; the family bleeds but holds.

chapters.title: Eye of the Storm
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Trapped in the lagoon as the monsoon's eye passes overhead, the crew plans the impossible: take the Pelican into the storm's tail to reach Halloran's salvage barge before it lifts the bullion. Nell, patched but weak, insists on steering. Beat: grief transmuted into purpose; all in.

chapters.title: Into the Tail
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The Pelican rides the monsoon's trailing edge toward the barge — masts groaning, pumps failing, Pili lashed to the wheel with Nell shouting courses. They arrive half-drowned as Halloran's divers begin the lift. Beat: peak peril; courage against indifferent nature.

chapters.title: The Last Dive
chapters.summary: Bram and Mara's POV, alternating underwater. While Halloran's men fight the storm topside, Bram and Mara dive to rig the bullion hold — not to steal it, but to collapse it onto the evidence vault, sealing the manifests in a tomb no one can quietly open. Halloran himself arrives by helicopter. Beat: the choice made — justice over treasure.

chapters.title: Halloran's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Climax, Bram's POV. Confrontation on the barge: Halloran offers Bram everything — the gold, the navy's protection, a life ashore. Bram detonates the charges; the hold collapses, taking the proof down with the wreck, while Mara broadcasts the copied manifests to every port authority and newsroom in the Pacific. Halloran's empire begins to drown in daylight. Beat: catharsis; the promise kept.

chapters.title: After the Water
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Aftermath: warrants dissolved as the manifests go public, Crane arrested, the navy's silence order collapsing under scrutiny. Nell recovers; Tui, broken by guilt, stays to rebuild the Pelican. Bram and Mara stand on the quarterdeck with nothing left to run from. Beat: exhale; debts paid, futures opened.

chapters.title: Passage and Current
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, coda. Months later, the Pelican works honest salvage under Nell's flag, Pili at the helm studying for her ticket. On the anniversary of Wren's death they pour rum into the sea over the Meridian's grave. Bram finally stops moving. Beat: rest earned; love and family as the true salvage.
